Here's what I found before I start changing things — there's a real trade-off the user should know about.

**Current state:**
- The "USB file transfer" screen is wired into the menu and has a state machine, but it's **entirely fake** — `enableUSBStorage()` just runs a 0→100% timer and prints "USB storage enabled". No TinyUSB, no MSC, no host-visible device. That's why the SD card never appears on a computer.
- `usb_transfer_todo.md` claims "COMPLETED ✅" but the implementation is simulated.

**What's actually needed for a real implementation:**
1. **Replace the fake state machine with the real `USBMSC` class** (`<USB.h>` + `<USBMSC.h>` are part of arduino-esp32 already, and `CONFIG_TINYUSB_MSC_ENABLED=1` is set in the framework). Read/write callbacks would call `SD.readRAW()` / `SD.writeRAW()` to expose the SD card as a sector device.
2. **Stop the SD loggers and `SD.end()` while MSC is active** so the host's writes aren't fighting the firmware's FAT cache, then re-mount when MSC is disabled.
3. **The blocker — USB mode**: the `m5stack-cores3` board variant defines `-DARDUINO_USB_MODE=1` (Hardware CDC/JTAG). In that mode the TinyUSB stack is *never initialized*, so `USBMSC.begin()` is a no-op. We have to override the build flag to `ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0` (TinyUSB) in `platformio.ini`. Side effect: `Serial` becomes USBCDC instead of HWCDC. Upload + monitor still work, but ROM bootloader interaction can differ slightly. The CoreS3 community uses TinyUSB mode for this exact feature, so it's well-trodden.

**Proposal:**
- Override `ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0` for the `m5stack-cores3-unified` env (keep CDC-on-boot so Serial console still works).
- Rewrite `usb_transfer_screen.cpp` to actually instantiate `USBMSC`, hook `onRead`/`onWrite`/`onStartStop` to `SD.readRAW`/`SD.writeRAW`, and start `USB.begin()` on demand.
- Stop SD loggers and `SD.end()` on Enable; restart on Disable.
- Keep the existing UI/progress phases, but tie them to real init steps instead of arbitrary timers.
- Core1/Core2 envs (ESP32 classic, no native USB) → keep the screen showing "Not supported on this board".

Want me to go ahead with this? The one thing to be aware of is the `ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0` switch — it changes Serial transport. If you've ever had upload/monitor weirdness on CoreS3 boards, you may want to flash a test build first. I can also try it as an opt-in flag (only when entering the screen) but the build flag itself is compile-time, so it's all-or-nothing per firmware.

**Changes**
- [platformio.ini](platformio.ini): override the CoreS3 variant's `ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1` (HW USB-CDC/JTAG) with `ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0` (TinyUSB) so the MSC interface can actually be registered. CDC-on-boot stays on, just routed through TinyUSB now.

- [bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/usb_transfer_screen.cpp](bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/usb_transfer_screen.cpp): rewrite to use the real `USBMSC` class.
  - Static `USBMSC g_usb_msc;` registers the MSC interface at C++ init time, before `app_main()` calls `USB.begin()`.
  - `usb_msc_read_cb` / `usb_msc_write_cb` loop over `SD.readRAW()` / `SD.writeRAW()` to handle multi-sector transfers (host can request more than one sector at a time).

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat: real USB MSC mass-storage transfer for CoreS3

Replace the simulated USB MSC state machine with a working TinyUSB
implementation that exposes the SD card to a host over USB-C.

- Override ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0 (TinyUSB) for m5stack-cores3 in
  platformio.ini, since the board variant defaults to HW USB-CDC/JTAG
  which makes USBMSC.begin() a no-op.
- Wire USBMSC read/write callbacks to SD.readRAW/writeRAW. Static
  USBMSC instance is registered at C++ init time so the MSC interface
  is in place before app_main() runs USB.begin().
- Add SDInterface::lock_for_msc/unlock_for_msc/force_remount.
  sd_diskio has no mutex protection between FATFS calls (main loop)
  and raw block I/O (TinyUSB task), so we lock SDInterface while MSC
  is active to keep firmware-side SD ops out of the SPI bus.
  force_remount bypasses the 5-second begin() rate limiter so a
  quick enable/disable cycle can refresh the FAT cache cleanly.
- Drop required_sd on the screen — the framework would otherwise
  paint NO SD CARD INSERTED while we hold the lock. Drive the state
  machine on every render tick (not gated on force) and force redraws
  while transitioning so the progress bar actually advances.
- Diagnostics via Serial.printf so they show in the monitor without
  needing CORE_DEBUG_LEVEL bumped.
- Core1/Core2 builds remain compilable; the screen falls back to
  "USB MSC not supported on this board" since classic ESP32 has no
  native USB peripheral.
